answer: At the wellhead a meter reads the steam flow, and the readings are logged every month in the station book, signed by the meter reader. A garden reading copied from another well fails the book: at the pearl of the meter the flow must match the well's own pressure, and a copied reading belongs to another well. Faking a year's readings means bribing the meter reader, forging twelve entries and paying 9,800, while the delta book in the station office is kept for the life of the well, so a reading whose meter was never read is struck off.
